messages.subject: Non-normal Phenotypes
parts:
Hi there,

I was wondering if you had any advice for dealing with non-normal phenotypes in RQTL2. I've tried to adapt the EM scan from RQTL for RQTL2 but haven't been successful.

Thanks for your time!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Non-normal Phenotypes
parts: I was wondering if you had any advice for dealing with non-normal phenotypes in RQTL2. I've tried to adapt the EM scan from RQTL for RQTL2 but haven't been successful.

In what way non-normal?

The usual options are:
- just use the standard analysis
- do some sort of transformation (log, square-root, or take ranks and then convert to normal quantiles)
- use a specialized model, like a generalized linear model

R/qtl2 currently just has normal model or analysis for binary traits.

The EM-based scan in R/qtl is for a normal model; it differs from Haley-Knott regression just in the treatment of missing genotype information. But it doesn't really help with the issue of non-normal phenotypes.

karl

parts: Oh I see, I have some data that is not normally distributed even after transformation. I thought that EM was a non-parametric scan for non-normal data but I see what you are saying. Thanks so much!
